then.text: You climb back up through the hatch into the ventilation shaft exit passage.
You duck down and squeeze back into the ventilation shaft opening. The metal groans under your weight.
The shaft behind you exhales stale, warm air. At least it's warmer than this bay.

objects.description: The ventilation hatch you came through, in the ceiling above.

objects.name: Torn Railing
objects.description: A section of walkway railing has been torn away, leaving a gap over the drainage pit below. Organic conduits run along the ceiling above.

then.text: The walkway railing is torn apart here — twisted metal and shredded organic cabling hanging over a gap. Below, the drainage pit drops into darkness. Above, thick conduits run along the ceiling toward the cataloguer's alcove. The gap is too wide to step across, but with the right tool you might be able to hook onto those overhead conduits and swing across.

interactions.response: The gap in the walkway. You crossed it once — you can cross it again.

then.text: You brace yourself and leap across the gap. For a moment you're airborne — then your feet hit the far edge. The surface is slick with drainage fluid. Your boots slide. Your hands claw at nothing. You fall backward into the drainage pit, tumbling through the dark until the impact drives the air from your lungs. The last thing you see is the amber fluid closing over your face.

then.title: A Fatal Leap
then.message: You tried to jump across the gap without any way to steady yourself. The wet surface offered no grip. Perhaps you should have found a tool to help you cross safely.

interactions.response: You grab the overhead conduit and swing across the gap again. Easier the second time.

then.text: You extend the surgical probe upward and hook its curved tip around the overhead conduit. It holds. You grip the probe's handle with both hands, kick off the walkway edge, and swing across the gap. Your feet find solid metal on the other side. The conduit groans but supports your weight. You unhook the probe — still intact, still useful. Now you can reach the cataloguer robot and its specimen jars.

You loop the neural tendril around the stub of torn railing on the far side. The organic fibers grip the metal like a living rope. You test it with your weight — it stretches but holds. You swing across the gap, feet landing on solid walkway. The tendril tightens its grip on the railing, forming a permanent handhold. Now you can reach the cataloguer and its specimen jars.

interactions.response: You've already crossed the gap. The overhead conduits are within reach now.
You've already crossed the gap. No need for the tendril.
The gap is too wide to just walk across. You need a way to reach the other side safely.
You stare into the drainage pit below. It doesn't answer. Neither does the gap.

objects.name: Metal Walkway
objects.description: A walkway runs between the pod racks. The metal is warm and slightly flexible.

then.text: A walkway runs between the pod racks. The metal has an organic quality — slightly warm, with a texture like tree bark. Grown, not forged. Drainage channels run along both sides, collecting the amber fluid that seeps from damaged pods.
The railing flexes slightly under your grip, like gripping a thick branch. It's sturdy enough, but the organic warmth is unsettling.

objects.name: Anatomy Display
objects.description: A large holographic screen showing detailed anatomical cross-sections.

then.text: Detailed anatomical cross-sections of... you. A goblin's entire nervous system mapped in glowing green lines. Organs catalogued, bone structure measured, pain receptors highlighted in red. They've been studying your kind. Thoroughly.

You study the holographic display. More species — dozens of them, each mapped in clinical detail. Your entry has a small symbol in the corner that matches the labels on the pods. A specimen number. You've been catalogued.

"I'm not just a number," you mutter at the display. The hologram flickers, cycling to a page of behavioral observations. Apparently, talking to inanimate objects is noted as 'common stress response in specimen 7G.'

objects.name: Restraint Straps
objects.description: Leather-like straps on the examination table, worn smooth by struggling.

then.text: Thick straps bolted to the examination table, worn smooth by years of struggling. The buckles are sized for something much larger than you — but smaller buckle holes have been punched in recently. Your size.
You test the straps. They're impossibly strong — some kind of bioengineered material. Whatever was held here fought hard and long, and still couldn't break free.

objects.name: Open Drawer
objects.description: A drawer pulled open at floor level. Something is inside.

then.text: Your blood runs cold. Lying in the drawer is a goblin. Like you. Dead — for some time, by the look of it. The eyes are open, staring at nothing. Surgical marks run across its chest, precise and methodical. You weren't the first specimen to wake up.

The dead goblin lies still in its drawer. The surgical precision of the marks on its chest tells you everything about what the Choir do to their specimens. Whatever happened to this one... you won't let it happen to you.

You reach into the drawer and find — a body. A goblin, like you. Dead. You gently close its eyes. The skin is cold but not rigid. It hasn't been dead that long. You weren't the first to wake up here. And the first one didn't make it.
You've already closed its eyes. There's nothing more you can do for it. But you can make sure their sacrifice wasn't meaningless — you'll find a way out.
"I'll get out," you whisper to the still form. "For both of us." The silence in the morgue feels heavier than before.

objects.name: Overturned Chair
objects.description: An overturned chair with a snapped leg, lying on its side.

then.text: The chair is overturned, one leg snapped clean off. Deep scratch marks gouge the floor beneath it — something was dragged away from this spot. The security operator didn't leave willingly.
You right the chair. Underneath, scratch marks are gouged deep into the floor — five parallel lines, like claws. Or fingers, desperately gripping as their owner was dragged away.

objects.name: Dark Crystal Rack
objects.description: The right wall holds crystals that are darker, almost black.

then.text: These crystals are darker than the ones on the left — almost black, with deep violet cores. The labels are different too. Not species data or collection records. Personal logs? Mission reports? Whatever these contain, it's not meant for the specimens.
You try to pull one free, but these are locked in place — unlike the left rack. Whatever's stored here, the Choir considered it important enough to secure.

objects.name: Stone Benches
objects.description: Two worn benches flanking the central pedestal.

then.text: Two seats, worn smooth by long use. The indentations suggest the Choir sat here regularly, reviewing their collection. Studying the worlds they'd stripped bare. There's something almost meditative about the arrangement — a chapel to their own conquest.

You sit down. The bench adjusts slightly to your weight — it's organic, like everything else on this ship. From here, the holographic display is perfectly framed. A front-row seat to the end of worlds.

objects.name: Enclosure Monitors
objects.description: Small screens above each energy barrier enclosure showing specimen data.

then.text: Vital signs, feeding schedules, behavioral notes — all in alien script. But the numbers are universal. These creatures have been here for years. Decades, some of them. The one in the middle enclosure has a note that translates roughly to 'communicative — further study warranted.'

You tap one of the screens. It cycles through data — weight, metabolism, aggression index. The middle enclosure's occupant is flagged as 'sapient, cooperative.' That creature can think. It might be able to help.

objects.name: Caged Creature
objects.description: A creature pacing behind the middle energy barrier. It watches you with intelligent, sorrowful eyes.

then.text: Behind the middle energy barrier, a creature paces in a tight circle. It's roughly your height but lean and angular, with mottled grey-blue skin and four arms folded against its torso. Its eyes — large, dark, and unmistakably intelligent — track your every move. The monitor above its cell reads 'sapient, cooperative.' This one can think. It might be able to communicate.

The Keth-Vari watches you through the barrier. Its four arms gesture slowly — a greeting, perhaps, or a plea. After your conversation, there's a connection between you. Two prisoners on the same ship, both far from home.
You reach toward the barrier. Static crackles and the hair on your arm stands up. The creature shakes its head urgently — no. It's seen what the barrier does to things that touch it.

The creature stops pacing and approaches the barrier. It makes a series of clicking sounds, then tilts its head, waiting. When you don't respond, it tries different sounds — whistles, hums, a deep thrumming. Then it touches two of its hands together and points at you, then at itself. A universal gesture: you and me. Same.

then.prompt: The creature waits, watching you with those dark, intelligent eyes. It pointed at you, then itself. Same. What do you say?

then.text: The creature's four arms spread wide — a gesture that somehow clearly means 'yes, exactly.' It presses two hands against the barrier space and makes a low, mournful sound. Then it points to the corridor exit and makes a running motion with its lower arms. Escape. It's telling you to go. To do what it can't.

choices.label: "Do you know a way out of here?"

then.text: The creature cocks its head, processing your tone. It points upward with one arm, then makes a sweeping gesture — the ship. With its other arms, it traces a path: left, forward, down. Then it mimics an opening motion, like doors parting. The airlock. It knows the layout — it's been here long enough to memorize every sound, every vibration through the walls. It taps the barrier and makes a frustrated sound. Trapped. But you're not.

choices.label: "What are they? The ones who put us here?"

then.text: The creature shudders, all four arms wrapping around itself. It makes a sound like grinding stone — disgust? Fear? It holds up three fingers and mimes something large, something that moves through walls. Then it points to the organic veins running through the ceiling and makes an encompassing gesture. The ship. The captors. They're the same thing. The Choir aren't just ON this ship — they ARE the ship.

You simply nod. The creature nods back — an eerily human gesture it must have learned from watching specimens. For a long moment, you just look at each other through the shimmering barrier. Two strangers from opposite ends of the galaxy, sharing the same cage. It touches its chest, then points at you. Remember me. Then it returns to pacing.

The creature presses its hands against the barrier space, mirroring your position. It makes a soft thrumming sound — comforting, like a lullaby from a world you'll never see. It can't help you escape, but it wants you to know you're not alone. Not anymore.

The creature traces the path again — left, forward, down. The airlock. It adds a new gesture: a fist opening slowly. The key. You need a key. It points toward the corridor and makes a stern, official-looking pose. Security. The key is somewhere in the security area.

The creature makes the grinding-stone sound again and gestures at the walls, the ceiling, the floor. All connected. All alive. It holds up its hands and makes a harvesting motion — scooping, collecting. The Choir harvest entire species. Your world, its world, dozens of others. All specimens in a collection that spans galaxies.
The creature stops pacing when it sees you. It touches its chest again. Remember me. Then it returns to its circuit. There's nothing more to say. But you won't forget.

You squeeze the nutrient paste through the energy barrier's flickering gap at floor level. The creature watches, then carefully picks up the tube. It sniffs, tastes, then devours the contents with desperate hunger. When it finishes, it looks at you with those large dark eyes and places all four hands against the barrier. A gesture of gratitude that needs no translation. The bond between you strengthens — you're not just fellow prisoners now. You're allies.

objects.name: Bio-Organic Keypad
objects.description: A fleshy keypad next to the main display. Four input slots glow faintly, awaiting a code sequence.

then.text: A bio-organic keypad with four input slots, each glowing a dull amber. The symbols on each key resemble numbers — or what passes for numbers in the Choir's notation. You'd need a specific four-digit code to activate this console.
The keypad glows green — code accepted. The console is active and ready for commands.

You press buttons at random. The keypad flashes red and emits a harsh buzz — wrong code. The ship's security system logs the failed attempt. You'd better find the right code before you trigger a lockout.

You enter the code from the specimen data plates: 7-3-1-9. The keypad pulses green. The console hums to life — screens sharpen, surveillance feeds stabilize. But the main override controls are still locked behind a physical lever. One step at a time.

You try to pry open the keypad with the surgical probe, hoping to bypass it. The probe slides into a seam — and the keypad's bio-organic membrane clamps down on it. The ship's immune system treats the probe as an intrusion. You yank it free before the membrane dissolves it. Brute force won't work here. You need the code.

interactions.response: "7... 3... 1... 9?" you mutter, trying to remember if those were the numbers on the specimen plates. You need to be sure before you try.
The keypad is embedded in the console's living surface. It can't be removed.

objects.name: Override Lever
objects.description: A heavy bio-mechanical lever behind a protective membrane. The main containment override.

then.text: A heavy lever behind a thick bio-organic membrane — the main containment override control. The membrane is sealed tight; it won't open until the console is active. Even then, pulling this lever will be loud. Very loud. Whatever is patrolling this deck will notice.

The membrane has retracted. The lever is exposed — a thick organic handle connected to the ship's containment lock system. Pulling it will override every containment lock on this deck. Including the ventilation shaft grate in the corridor.

You push against the membrane. It's rubbery and warm, giving slightly under your hands but refusing to tear. The lever behind it is tantalizingly close. You need to activate the console first — the membrane retracts when the system is online.

You grab the lever with both hands and pull. It resists — then gives with a wet, organic crack. Across the deck, you hear the deep thunk of containment locks disengaging. Every secured door, every grated vent, every sealed passage on this level just opened. The surveillance feeds show the Curator pausing mid-stride, head tilting. It knows. You've just made a lot of noise — but you've also opened every path forward.
The lever is locked in the pulled position. All containment locks on this deck are open. There's no putting them back.

You try to cut through the membrane with the surgical probe. The tip pierces the surface, but the membrane heals almost instantly — the ship's regeneration is too fast. You need to get the console active so the membrane retracts on its own.

interactions.response: "Containment override," you read from the console label. "One pull and every lock on this deck opens. No going back."
The lever is anchored deep in the console's internal structure. It moves in one direction only — and that's a big decision.

objects.name: Key Card Drawer
objects.description: A small drawer beneath the console, jammed partially open. Key cards glint inside.

then.text: A drawer jammed half-open — probably from whatever fight happened here. Inside, you can see bio-organic key cards in various shades, each pulsing faintly with embedded circuitry. These are access cards for different sections of the containment deck.
You pull out a key card — it pulses like a heartbeat in your palm. Bio-organic circuitry embedded in compressed cartilage. This should open any standard containment door on the ship.

interactions.response: You already have a key card. The remaining ones are a different clearance level — too high for you.
A faint label above the drawer slot — three alien glyphs and what looks like a security clearance level. The lowest tier, if you're reading the hierarchy right.
The drawer slides on organic rails but won't detach from the console. It's grown into the structure.

objects.name: Surveillance Feeds
objects.description: Multiple screens showing surveillance feeds from across the containment deck.

then.text: The surveillance screens show mostly static — the console needs to be activated before they'll show anything useful. You can make out flickering shapes behind the noise, but nothing clear.

The feeds sharpen with the console active. You see: the corridor, empty. The feeding station, cages glowing. The processing lab, dark. And there — a tall figure moving with mechanical precision through a distant passageway. The Curator, making its rounds. It's methodical, predictable. You could time your movements around its patrol pattern.
The surveillance feeds show the Curator's patrol route. It moves through the outer corridors in a clockwise pattern, pausing at each containment cell. Its route doesn't include this room — for now.

interactions.response: You tap the screens. They're organic display panels — warm to the touch, slightly yielding. The feeds flicker but don't change.
"Show me where it is," you whisper to the screens. They don't respond to voice commands. This is a security console, not a personal assistant.

objects.name: System Status Display
objects.description: A readout showing the current status of the containment deck's systems.

interactions.response: The status display is dark — the console needs power before it will show anything.

then.text: The status display comes alive with alien readouts. You can parse the basics: containment locks ENGAGED across all sections. Ventilation grates SEALED. Specimen counts for each cell. And a deck map — the full layout of this level. You memorize the important bits: the ventilation shaft connects the corridor to the airlock bay. If you could get the vent grate open...

interactions.response: The status display shows all containment locks DISENGAGED. Red warning symbols pulse across the map. You've opened everything.
The display is a projection surface — your hand passes through the holographic readouts, disrupting them momentarily.
You read the alien symbols aloud, trying to sound out the Choir's language. It sounds like grinding stones. Nothing responds.

objects.name: Emergency Override
objects.description: A red emergency button that appeared after the ship's processing terminal was accessed.

then.text: A red emergency override button — it wasn't glowing before. Accessing the processing terminal must have activated emergency protocols across the ship's network. The medic cross symbol suggests this is a containment safety override. Press it to disengage the deck's containment locks.

You press the emergency override button. It sinks into the console with a wet click — and across the deck, containment locks disengage with a series of heavy thunks. Every secured door, every grated vent, every sealed passage on this level just opened. The surveillance feeds flicker. Whatever patrols these corridors will notice. But every path forward is now open.

interactions.response: The override button is dark now — all containment locks are already disengaged. There's nothing left to override.
It's a button. It doesn't talk back.

objects.name: Shaft Ahead
objects.description: The ventilation shaft continues forward into branching darkness.

then.text: The shaft ahead splits into multiple directions. Red emergency lights flicker in the distance.
You crawl forward through the ventilation shaft. The walls pulse faintly, alive. Ahead, the tunnel opens into a junction.
You feel the warm air flowing from ahead. The shaft beckons.
Your voice echoes down the shaft and comes back distorted.

objects.name: Wall Markings
objects.description: Scratch marks at the junction where the vent splits.

then.text: Scratches on the walls at the junction. They might mean something, but without context they're just random gouges in the organic material.

Cross-referencing with your map: the LEFT tunnel is marked with a small helmet symbol — hazardous but the correct path toward the airlock. The RIGHT tunnel is scored with deep warning gouges — a dead end. The mapmaker was thorough.
You run your fingers over the scratches. They're deep — made with desperate force.
"Which way..." The tunnels swallow your whisper without echo.

objects.name: Overhead Pipes
objects.description: Bio-organic pipes running along the ceiling of the junction.

then.text: Thick bio-organic pipes run along the ceiling, branching where the tunnel splits. They pulse faintly — the ship's circulatory system. The left branch carries pipes that hiss with chemical vapor. The right branch's pipes are dry and cracked.
The pipes are warm and faintly sticky. You pull your hand away quickly.
The pipes gurgle in response, like a stomach digesting.

objects.name: Air Current
objects.description: You can feel different air currents from each tunnel.

then.text: The air behaves differently at the junction. From the LEFT, warm air carries a sharp chemical smell — acrid, metallic, wrong. From the RIGHT, the air is stale and dead — no circulation, as if the tunnel ends.
You hold your hand up to feel the currents. Left: warm, chemical-tinged, with a faint mechanical vibration. Right: still, stale, motionless.
You sniff the air. The left tunnel smells dangerous. The right smells like nothing at all.

objects.name: Left Tunnel
objects.description: The left branch of the junction. A faint yellow-green haze drifts from it.

then.text: The left tunnel stretches into a yellowish haze. Something chemical hangs in the air. It could be dangerous… or it could be nothing.
Your map marks this as the correct path. The helmet symbol means you'll need protection. The chemical haze confirms it — toxic gas ahead.
You crawl into the left tunnel. The air grows warmer, sharper. A yellow-green haze thickens around you.
The walls of the left tunnel are slick with chemical condensation.
Your voice sounds muffled in the thickening air of the left tunnel.

objects.name: Right Tunnel
objects.description: The right branch of the junction. Darker and narrower than the left.

then.text: The right tunnel is narrower and darker. The air from it is completely still.
Your map marks this tunnel with deep warning gouges. Dead end. But someone made it that far… there might be something worth finding.
You squeeze into the narrower right tunnel. The walls close in. The air is stale and dead.
The walls of the right tunnel are dry and cracked. No moisture, no life.
Your voice falls flat in the dead air of the right tunnel. No echo at all.

objects.name: Back to Entry
objects.description: The tunnel back to the ventilation shaft entry.

then.text: The tunnel leads back to the ventilation shaft entrance where you climbed in.
You crawl back to the vent shaft entry. The faint glow of the corridor above is reassuring.
You brace against the walls as you back up.
"Maybe I should go back and prepare..."

objects.name: Cracked Pipe
objects.description: A bio-organic pipe split open, leaking toxic yellow-green vapor.

then.text: A thick bio-organic pipe has split open like a wound, its dark flesh peeled back to reveal a luminous interior. Yellow-green vapor pours from the breach in steady pulses, synchronized with the ship's breathing rhythm. The gas is clearly toxic — the dissolved remains nearby prove that.
You reach toward the pipe and immediately pull back. The gas burns your skin on contact. You need protection before touching anything in here.

With the helmet protecting you, you examine the pipe up close. The breach is organic — the ship's flesh tore open here, probably from the same impact that damaged the stasis hold. There's no way to seal it.
The gas hisses from the pipe like a warning. The ship exhales poison here.

objects.name: Dissolved Remains
objects.description: The partially dissolved remains of a large creature.

then.text: A specimen larger than the one in the entry shaft. This creature made it further into the maze before the gas stopped it. The body is partially dissolved — the toxic vapor has been eating at it for months. A Choir uniform clings to what's left of the torso.
You lean closer to examine the body. The gas burns your eyes, your throat, your lungs—

then.message: The toxic gas overwhelms you. Your vision blurs, your lungs seize. You collapse beside the remains, another specimen who didn't make it through the vents.
then.title: Toxic Death

then.text: With the helmet sealing out the gas, you can examine the body safely. A Choir crew member, judging by the uniform. They were trying to escape their own ship. Their personnel badge is too corroded to read. Whatever they knew about the vent system, they didn't have protection for this section.
"You almost made it," you whisper to the remains. The gas swirls around them like a shroud.

objects.name: Tunnel Ahead
objects.description: The tunnel continues through the gas toward a distant mechanical sound.

then.text: The tunnel continues forward through the thickest part of the gas. You can hear a distant mechanical grinding from somewhere ahead. You can't survive walking through that concentration without some kind of breathing protection.
The tunnel continues through the gas. With the helmet, you could survive the passage. Beyond the haze, you hear a rhythmic mechanical grinding.
You push deeper into the gas. Your eyes water. Your throat closes. You can't breathe—

then.message: Without protection, the toxic gas overwhelms you in seconds. Your lungs burn, your vision fails. You stumble and fall, another victim of the ship's poisoned veins.
then.title: Toxic Death

then.text: The helmet's visor seals automatically as you push through the densest gas. It sits like a fishbowl on your shoulders, but the internal atmosphere system keeps you breathing clean air. You emerge on the other side into a chamber dominated by a massive spinning fan.
You feel the air current pushing against you from deeper in the tunnel. Something mechanical is moving a lot of air ahead.
The grinding sound from ahead reverberates through the gas-filled tunnel.

objects.name: Back to Junction
objects.description: The tunnel back to the junction.

then.text: The tunnel back to the junction. The air is cleaner that direction.
You retreat from the gas back to the junction. The air clears as you crawl.
You brace against the walls, backing away from the toxic haze.
"I need to find another way… or get protection."

objects.name: Ventilation Fan
objects.description: A massive ventilation fan blocks the entire passage.

then.text: A massive ventilation fan fills the entire tunnel cross-section, its five dark metal blades spinning at lethal speed. The wind pushes against you with physical force. Through the blur of the blades, you can see the tunnel continuing on the other side. Nothing could pass through alive while it's running.

The fan blades are locked in place, frozen mid-rotation. Your surgical probe is wedged deep into the mechanism, bent beyond recovery but doing its job. There's enough gap between the stilled blades to squeeze through.
You'd lose your arm. The blades are moving far too fast — they'd cut through flesh and bone before you registered the impact.
The stilled blades are solid cold metal. They won't move while the probe holds. You could squeeze between them.
You push against the wind toward the spinning blades. A blade catches you—

then.message: The fan blade strikes with the force of a freight train. Your adventure ends instantly in the spinning dark of the ventilation shaft.
then.title: Fan Death

then.text: You carefully squeeze between the jammed fan blades, turning sideways to fit through the narrow gaps. The metal is cold against your skin. On the other side, the air is fresher. You're through.
The fan drowns out your voice with its rhythmic whooshing. WHUMP. WHUMP. WHUMP.
In the silence of the stopped fan, you can hear your own breathing and the distant hum of the ship.

objects.name: Fan Mechanism
objects.description: The fan's exposed drive mechanism on the wall.

then.text: The fan's drive mechanism is exposed — bio-organic muscle tissue wrapped around a metal axle, pulsing with effort as it drives the massive blades. A narrow gap in the housing could accept a tool to jam the gears. Something long, thin, and strong enough to wedge into the mechanism.
Your surgical probe is wedged firmly in the mechanism's gears. The bio-organic muscle tissue still strains against the obstruction, but the probe holds. It's bent and useless for anything else now.
The mechanism is too powerful to stop by hand. The bio-organic muscles driving it could tear your arm off. You need a tool — something to wedge into that gap in the housing.
The probe is locked in place. You couldn't extract it even if you wanted to.

You wedge the surgical probe into the mechanism's gears. Metal grinds against bio-tissue — the fan stutters, shudders, and LOCKS. The sudden silence is deafening. The probe is bent beyond recovery, but the blades are stopped. You can squeeze through now.
That won't fit in the mechanism gap. You need something long, thin, and sturdy enough to jam the gears.
The mechanism pulses with a biological rhythm. The ship's muscles drive the fan like a heartbeat drives blood.

objects.name: Back Through Gas
objects.description: The tunnel back through the gas chamber.

then.text: The tunnel leads back through the gas-filled chamber to the junction.
You crawl back through the gas. The helmet keeps you breathing safely.
You crawl back into the gas. Without the helmet, the fumes burn your eyes and throat—

then.message: The toxic gas overwhelms you on the return trip. Without the helmet that got you through before, you have no protection. Your lungs give out halfway back.
then.title: Toxic Death

then.text: You brace yourself for the return trip through the toxic section.
"Back through the gas..."

objects.name: Collapsed Rubble
objects.description: The ceiling has caved in, completely blocking the passage.

then.text: The ceiling has collapsed completely, sealing the passage with tons of rubble and twisted metal. The ship's organic material has grown OVER the debris like scar tissue — this collapse happened long ago and the living ship partially healed around it. There's no getting through.
You push against the rubble. It doesn't budge. The ship's organic growth has fused it into a solid mass. This passage is permanently sealed.
There's no way through. The collapse is absolute.
Your voice bounces off the rubble wall and returns flat. No space beyond it.

objects.name: Skeletal Figure
objects.description: The skeleton of a large alien creature propped against the rubble.

then.text: A skeletal figure sits propped against the rubble, too large for a human. Angular bones, elongated skull — this was a Choir crew member. They were trying to escape their own ship. In their bony hands, a datapad still faintly glows, its screen casting pale blue-white light across the dead face.
Without the datapad's glow, you notice something else — a faint pulsing light beneath the skeleton's uniform collar. Something small, crystalline, tucked into a chest pocket. A security chip?
You carefully extract the datapad from the skeleton's grip. The bones creak but don't resist. The screen flickers — it still has charge. A Choir crew member's last record.

You reach into the skeleton's chest pocket and extract a small crystalline chip. It pulses warmly in your hand — a Choir security clearance badge, still active. This engineer's bio-signature is stored inside. Whoever they were, their clearance might open doors deeper in the ship.
The skeleton has nothing left to offer. You've taken the datapad and the security chip — everything useful from this dead engineer's last journey.

The skeleton sits empty-handed and stripped of valuables. A Choir engineer who died trying to escape through the same vents you're crawling through now. At least their security chip might still be useful.
"You were trying to get out too," you whisper to the remains. "How long ago? How many have tried?"

objects.name: Wall Scratches
objects.description: Scratch marks on the walls near the skeleton.

then.text: More scratches on the walls. These look more frantic than the ones at the entry — deep, desperate gouges. The marks of someone who realized they'd chosen wrong.

These match the warning marks on your map. Whoever scratched the map in the entry shaft came here first, found the dead end, then went back and left warnings for the next escape attempt. The mapmaker and this skeleton might not be the same person.
Deep enough to feel the desperation. Claws, not tools — made by an alien, not a human.
"Dead end. Just like the map warned." The words feel hollow in the sealed passage.

objects.name: Back to Junction
objects.description: The tunnel back to the junction.

then.text: The tunnel back to the junction. Nothing more to find here.
You crawl back to the junction. The dead end yields nothing more — except the datapad, if you took it.
You brace against the narrow walls as you back out.
"Nothing more here. Time to try the other way."

objects.name: Crack in Wall
objects.description: A crack in the vent wall revealing the void of space.

then.text: Through a crack in the vent wall, you see STARS. Pinpoints of light scattered across infinite black. The first time you've seen outside the ship. The void is beautiful and terrifying — you are very, very far from home. Cool blue starlight spills through the crack, the first light that isn't emergency red since you woke up.

You press your face to the crack. The hull is cold. Beyond it, nothing but vacuum and stars. The ship is adrift between worlds. You can see hull damage along the exterior — whatever hit this vessel hit it hard.
"Stars…" Your voice catches. You'd almost forgotten there was an outside. An anywhere that isn't this ship.

objects.name: Exit Hatch
objects.description: The vent shaft opens into a larger chamber below.

then.text: The ventilation shaft opens into a large chamber below. Through the hatch, you can see docking clamps, the curved interior hull of an airlock bay, and — is that a shuttle? The operational decks. Freedom, or at least the next step toward it.
You lower yourself through the hatch and drop into the airlock bay. The ceiling is high here, the space vast compared to the cramped vents. You've made it through.
The hatch rim is smooth — this was a maintenance access point, not an escape route. But it'll do.
"Almost there. Just a drop into the bay below."

objects.name: Back to Fan Room
objects.description: The tunnel back toward the fan.

then.text: The tunnel leads back to the fan room. The jammed blades are still passable.
You crawl back through the jammed fan blades to the fan room.
You brace yourself to squeeze back through the fan blades.
"Why would I go back? The airlock is right here."

objects.name: Emergency Equipment Cabinet
objects.description: A wall-mounted cabinet with a cracked glass front, marked with alien safety symbols.

then.text: A wall-mounted emergency equipment cabinet with a cracked glass front. Alien safety symbols are stenciled on it — what looks like a helmet icon and a breathing mask. The latch is stuck but the glass is already cracked. You could probably force it open.
The emergency cabinet hangs open, its cracked glass door askew. Most of the equipment inside is designed for Choir anatomy — far too large for you. The helmet slot is empty.

You smash through the cracked glass and wrench the cabinet open. Inside: emergency equipment designed for Choir anatomy — suits far too large, breathing apparatus you can't operate. But the helmet… the helmet has a universal seal. It sits like a fishbowl on your head, but it locks and the atmosphere system activates. This could protect you from toxic environments.
The cabinet is empty of anything useful. The remaining equipment is all Choir-sized.
The safety symbols on the cabinet are clear enough — helmet, breathing mask, protective gear. Universal concepts, even for aliens.
It's bolted to the wall.

on_solve.text: The bio-organic keypad pulses green. The lab door hisses open, releasing a waft of chemical-laced air.

on_fail.text: The keypad pulses red. A low warning tone sounds.

config.wrong_step_message: The sequence resets with an irritated buzz.

on_solve.text: The console flares to life. Surveillance feeds flicker across every screen — the ship is enormous. A schematic appears: deck layouts, containment sections, operational levels. You memorize what you can. The containment locks disengage with a distant clunk.

on_fail.text: Wrong sequence. The console buzzes and resets.

on_solve.text: The resonance tones harmonize. The bridge console activates, holographic star maps blooming into existence. Hundreds of systems — most marked in red. Consumed.

on_fail.text: Dissonant tones. The lock rejects the combination.

on_solve.text: The reactor's heartbeat shifts rhythm. Power surges to the shuttle bay — lights flicker on in that distant section. Alarms stay silent. For now.

on_fail.text: An alarm blares briefly before the system compensates. Wrong configuration.

on_solve.text: Static resolves into something alien — subsonic pulses carrying data you can't parse. But the recorder can. The ship's black box begins logging the Convergence's transmissions. Coordinates. Orders. The scope of their operation laid bare.

on_fail.text: A burst of static. Wrong frequency — the array whines in protest.

on_solve.text: The blast door groans open for the first time in decades. Emergency lighting flickers on inside — amber strips illuminating dust-covered corridors. The bunker still has power. Someone built this to last.

on_fail.text: The dials click but the door holds. Wrong combination.

config.correct_step_message: The crystal chimes and glows brighter.
config.wrong_step_message: The crystals dim and reset. A discordant tone echoes through the library.

on_solve.text: The crystals align in harmonic resonance. Data floods the reading station — centuries of research on the Convergence, its patterns, its weaknesses. Among the records: the fourth cipher fragment, the key to reading everything they wrote.
Generators hum to life. Lights flicker on in the chosen districts, casting long shadows through empty streets. The city stirs — and somewhere in the ruins, The Watcher takes notice.

on_fail.text: Overload. The grid sparks and resets. Too many districts for the remaining power.

on_solve.text: The resonance chamber thrums with ancient frequency. The murals glow — and from the altar, a crystal rises. Inside it: visions of possible futures. A weapon assembled. A bridge between minds. An escape into darkness. A warning cast to the stars. You see yourself in all of them.

on_fail.text: The chamber responds with a mournful drone. Wrong frequency.

on_solve.text: Seven tones lock into ancient harmony. The Convergence-era controls awaken — crystalline interfaces lighting up with patterns older than most civilizations. From here, the harvesting can be redirected. Stopped. Or overloaded.

on_fail.text: The Convergence-era lock rejects the combination with a crystalline screech.

on_solve.text: The crystalline antenna vibrates at a frequency that makes your bones ache. The galactic sweep mode engages — this signal will reach every inhabited system within range. Every world. Every species. The Convergence's own infrastructure turned into the galaxy's warning system.

on_fail.text: The array crackles with misdirected energy. Wrong calibration.

phases.name: Awakening

on_enter.text: Your eyes open to green light and the smell of chemicals. Fluid drains from your cracked stasis pod, pooling on the organic-metallic floor. You're cold. Weak. Alone among hundreds of pods holding dead things from a dozen worlds. Something hums in the walls — the ship is alive.

phases.ambient_text: The specimen hold hums with the heartbeat of a living ship. Pods glow faintly around you. Something clicks in a distant corridor.

phases.name: Containment Escape

on_enter.text: Containment locks disengage throughout the deck. New corridors open. The ship's layout starts to make sense — but so does the danger. The Curator's patrol pattern shifts. It knows something is wrong.

phases.ambient_text: Distant clicking. The Curator adjusts its rounds. You have more freedom now — and less time to use it.

phases.name: Infiltration

on_enter.text: The architecture shifts from clinical to alien. This is where the Choir lives. The walls are covered in geometric patterns. The air tastes different — alive, breathing. You are deep in enemy territory now.

phases.ambient_text: Subsonic resonance hums through the walls. The Choir communicates through vibration. You can feel their thoughts in your teeth.

phases.name: Shuttle Launch

on_enter.text: The shuttle's systems initialize. The bay door begins to open — stars and the planet's surface visible beyond. But the Curator has been alerted. Amber light sweeps the bay. You have seconds to launch.

phases.ambient_text: Alarms blare. The shuttle vibrates. The Curator's footsteps echo in the bay.

phases.name: Survival

on_enter.text: The shuttle hits the ground hard. You crawl from the wreckage into a world being murdered. Grey soil, dead trees frozen in crystal, a sky the wrong color. In the distance: the silhouette of a city. Above: energy beams draining the planet dry. You're free of the ship. You're not free.

phases.ambient_text: The wasteland is silent except for the crackle of siphon towers and the whisper of dead wind through crystallized trees.

phases.name: City Approach

on_enter.text: The city gates loom above you — massive, elegant, partially collapsed. Reliefs of four-armed figures watch you with empty eyes. Beyond: an intact city, abandoned. Lights still glow in some windows. Something moved inside. You're sure of it.

phases.ambient_text: Empty streets. Flickering lights. The echo of a civilization's last breath, caught in crystal.

phases.name: Investigation

on_enter.text: You step into the dead city. Everything is frozen mid-moment — a meal on a table, a vehicle stopped in the road, toys on a floor. The evacuation was sudden. The Echoes here are stronger, more coherent. And something new watches: a geometric shape of pure light drifting between the spires. The Convergence knows you're here.

phases.ambient_text: Ghostly figures flicker at the edges of vision. The Watcher's geometric glow passes behind buildings. The dead city remembers.

phases.name: Deep City

on_enter.text: The weapon vault opens. They built something to fight the Convergence — and they almost finished it. The components are here, scattered across secure containment units. The Watcher's patrols intensify. It's protecting something deeper. You're close.

phases.ambient_text: Crystal barriers grow where you've been. The Watcher restructures the city around you, funneling you away from secrets.

phases.name: Endgame

on_enter.text: You descend into the nexus. Reality bends. The walls are pure crystallized energy. Rivers of stolen life force flow past you toward the core. The planet's agony made visible. Everything you've gathered, everything you've learned — it comes down to what happens next.

phases.ambient_text: The nexus hums with the energy of a dying world. Every step forward is a step toward something that has consumed galaxies.

phases.name: Final Confrontation

on_enter.text: The core. A crystalline intelligence filling a spherical chamber, fractal and infinite. It perceives you. Visions flood your mind — consumed worlds, the Choir's creation, entropy advancing, a universe winding down. The Convergence speaks in stolen memories. It is afraid. It is merciless. And it is waiting for your choice.

phases.ambient_text: The core pulses with thought. Visions of dead worlds flicker across its surface. It knows what you carry. It knows what you can do.

effects.text: The last of the stasis fluid drains from your pod. You shiver. Around you, other pods glow with their preserved contents — some moving, most still.
Click. Click. Click. Somewhere far below, precise footsteps on metal grating. The Curator begins its rounds.
A pod near you rattles. Something inside twitches — alive, barely. Its eyes open, unfocused, and close again. Not all the specimens are dead.
The ship pulses. The bioluminescent veins in the walls brighten, then fade. Like a heartbeat. The ship is alive, and it just noticed something.
A change in the ship's resonance. The Curator's patrol pattern accelerates. It has found evidence of your passage. Amber light sweeps faster through the corridors.
A new sound: the skittering of small mechanical legs. Maintenance drones — spider-like automata — fan out from their charging stations. The Curator has deployed its assistants.

The viewport shows the planet in full. Energy siphons descend from orbit like needles. Where they touch, the surface blackens and dies. The planet's atmosphere is yellowing. It's being murdered slowly, and you're watching from the killer's house.
Smoke rises from the shuttle wreckage behind you. The beetle-shaped craft will never fly again. Above, the alien ship is a dark shape against the wrong-colored sky. You are alone on a dying world.

Reality stutters. A translucent figure materializes — tall, four-armed, wearing what might be a uniform. It walks three steps, stops, turns, and walks back. Again. Again. It doesn't see you. It's replaying its last moments. An Echo — a remnant of this world's consumed civilization, burned into the Convergence's energy field.

Collapsed shelters. Scattered belongings. A makeshift barricade facing the city — they tried to hold something back. And on the ground: skeletons. Tall, thin, four arms each. They tried to flee. They didn't make it. The silence here is heavier than anywhere else.

Something new. A geometric shape — a shifting polyhedron of pure light — drifts between the city's spires. It doesn't move like a living thing. It optimizes. The Watcher. The Convergence's eye in its own domain.

The room splits. Half decayed ruin, half living city as it was. The boundary shimmers and cracks. A ghostly scientist stands at a console in the pristine half, frozen mid-action. With the Echo Stabilizer, you can almost hear their voice: '...the weapon core must be shielded before assembly or the energy will...' The vision fractures.
The nexus surges. Energy flows brighten, the hum rises to a roar — the harvesting is accelerating. The planet is running out of time.

A distant boom. A Choir shuttle crashes into the crystallized landscape near the nexus entrance. Amber light emerges from the wreckage. The Curator. It followed you from orbit. It crash-landed a shuttle to pursue its escaped specimen across a dying world. Dedication or programming — does it matter?

It speaks. Not in words — in visions. Consumed worlds flash before your eyes: blue oceans turned to dust, forests crystallized, civilizations reduced to Echoes. Thousands of worlds. Millions of species. And beneath the horror, a deeper truth: the Convergence is afraid. The universe is winding down. Entropy is winning. It consumes to survive.
The visions fade. You stand before something older than most stars. It has shown you its fear. Now it waits for your answer.

A gallery of the damned. Specimens from the Convergence's first worlds — beings from billions of years ago, perfectly preserved in crystal. Species beyond imagination, each the last of its kind. And there — one of the four-armed planet inhabitants, frozen mid-scream, mouth open, eyes wide. They got this far. They saw what you're seeing. They didn't make it out.
The sky darkens further. The energy siphons are reaching critical extraction. The planet shudders. Whatever you're going to do, the time to do it is running out.

killer.name: The Curator
killer.description: A specialized Choir unit responsible for the specimen collection. Taller than standard Choir drones, with additional manipulator limbs and optical sensors that glow amber. It catalogues, preserves, and maintains specimens with obsessive precision. You are its most recent acquisition — and its first escape.

on_approach: Click. Click. Click. Precise footsteps on metal grating. Amber light sweeps the corridor ahead.
A subsonic hum vibrates through the walls. The Curator is near, performing its rounds.
The air shifts — something large moving through the corridor. Amber sensors glow in the darkness.
on_search: The Curator's manipulator limbs unfold, probing surfaces, checking specimens. Its optical sensors pan slowly, missing nothing.
It stops. Head tilts. The amber glow intensifies as it scans each corner of the room with mechanical precision.
Four limbs extend, each one testing a surface, a panel, a shadow. It searches the way a machine searches — without impatience, without error.
on_clear: The amber glow dims. The Curator retracts its limbs and continues its patrol. Click. Click. Click.
Satisfied — if a machine can be satisfied — it moves on. The footsteps fade.
on_evidence: The amber glow intensifies. The Curator pauses. Its head tilts — a mechanical gesture of recognition. It knows something is wrong.
A burst of subsonic resonance — the Curator communicating with the ship. It has found evidence. Protocols are updating.
It traces the disruption with one manipulator limb. Records it. Catalogs it. Then turns, amber sensors blazing, and begins a systematic search.
on_catch: Four manipulator limbs close around you with clinical precision. No pain — it doesn't want to damage its specimen. You are carried, struggling uselessly, back to a containment cell.

effects.text: A click echoes through the corridor. The Curator has relocked the lab door.
Metal scraping. The Curator has sealed the ventilation grate with something stronger than screws.
The lights in the shuttle bay section flicker and die. The Curator has overridden the power reroute.

special_behaviors.description: The Curator's movements slow. The sedative compound interferes with its biological components.

on_trigger_effects.text: The Curator staggers. Its movements slow, becoming erratic. The sedative is fighting its bio-mechanical systems. It won't last long.

special_behaviors.description: The overcharge device disrupts the Curator's resonance-based senses.

on_trigger_effects.text: The overcharge device detonates in a burst of resonance static. The Curator recoils, its sensors overwhelmed. Its amber lights flicker wildly.

special_behaviors.description: The Curator has been convinced of your sentience. It ceases hostilities and may assist.

on_trigger_effects.text: The Curator goes still. Its amber sensors dim, then shift — to blue. For the first time, it sees you not as a specimen, but as a person. It lowers its manipulator limbs. It will not hunt you again.

special_behaviors.description: Echoes manifest near the player, causing noise and disturbance.

on_trigger_effects.text: An Echo manifests — a translucent figure stuttering through reality. The disruption sends ripples through the energy field.

special_behaviors.description: The Watcher has detected the player and is restructuring the environment.

on_trigger_effects.text: The Watcher LOCKS onto your position. Crystal grows from the walls, sealing corridors behind you. The geometric shape shifts, its faces reorienting — each one a different sensor, all pointed at you.

win_conditions.description: Escape — 'The Survivor': Flee the system in a shuttle, leaving the planet to its fate. Hollow victory.
Destroy — 'The Sacrifice': Activate the countermeasure at the nexus heart. The planet is saved. You don't make it out.
Sabotage + Escape — 'The Best of Both': Set the countermeasure on a timer, then escape before it detonates. The golden ending.
Signal — 'The Warning': Hijack the transmission array to broadcast Convergence intel and weapon schematics to every inhabited system in range.
Kamikaze — 'The Hammer': Recall the Choir vessel and crash it into the nexus using reactivated orbital defense satellites. Pyrrhic victory — the planet is destroyed too.
Transcendence — 'The Bridge': Interface directly with the Convergence, merging with its intelligence to redirect its hunger. The harvesting stops everywhere. You cease to exist as a person.

lose_conditions.description: Caught by the Curator, an Echo, or a Convergence defense system. Returned to containment (Acts 1-2) or neutralized (Acts 3-5).

lose_conditions.message: The planet shudders one final time. The energy siphons reach critical mass. The surface cracks, continents splitting apart as the Convergence drains the last of the world's energy. The sky burns white. Then — silence. The harvest is complete.
lose_conditions.description: The planet is fully consumed before you can act.
